title: RapidAI automated LVO detection alerts Memorial Neuroscience Institute's stroke team; 29-year-old firefighter's artery reopened within 60 minutes of arrival
summary: RapidAI's large vessel occlusion alert prompted a physician to mobilize the stroke team for Eric, 29; thrombectomy restored flow under 60 minutes from arrival; no deficits.
account: Memorial Healthcare System began a RapidAI trial at Memorial Regional Hospital in 2017, according to its release. It then extended the platform to Memorial Hospital West, Memorial Hospital Miramar and Memorial Hospital Pembroke. Eric, a 29-year-old firefighter and paramedic, felt unwell after a workout. He tried to send a text and could not move his left thumb, then his left leg went numb. His trainer noticed that he was slurring and called 9-1-1. Emergency medical services (EMS) took him to Memorial Hospital West's Comprehensive Stroke Center. Under the Memorial stroke protocol the paramedics had already alerted the hospital. The neurointerventional surgery team was ready to do a computed tomography (CT) scan and treat in the catheterization laboratory. As soon as scan results were available, Dr Brijesh Mehta received the RapidAI alert on his smartphone and smartwatch. It showed the software's automated detection of a large vessel occlusion (LVO). The alert prompted him to mobilize the catheterization laboratory team and fast-track Eric for mechanical thrombectomy. The blocked artery was fully opened and blood flow restored under 60 minutes from his arrival. Eric described himself as alive with no deficits. The hospital published the account on 12 May 2022. The release gives neither the date nor the city of Eric's stroke, and it gives no measured time saved by the alert.
purpose: RapidAI's platform is built to detect large vessel occlusion on imaging and push alerts to the stroke team so that thrombectomy can start sooner. This is its intended function.
deployer: Memorial Healthcare System / Memorial Neuroscience Institute (Memorial Hospital West)
taxonomy_note: The AI's part was faster team mobilization, and EMS had already pre-notified the hospital, so the counterfactual is unproven.

ratings.reason: A 29-year-old had his occluded artery reopened within 60 minutes of arrival and reports being alive with no deficits. The AI's share is the time saved in fast-tracking the cath lab team after EMS had already pre-notified the hospital and the team was ready. The thrombectomy was the treatment.
Dr Mehta states that the platform streamlines workflow and cuts time compared with the previous need to open scans at workstations.

ai_role.statement: RapidAI's automated LVO detection delivered the alert that prompted Dr Mehta to mobilize the cath lab team and fast-track thrombectomy. Under the Memorial stroke protocol EMS had already pre-notified the hospital and the neurointerventional team was ready before imaging. The occlusion would have been identified on the CT scan regardless. So the AI's contribution is speed at the point of care, and its share of the time saved cannot be separated from the pre-notification. The only counterfactual offered is Dr Mehta's general description of the pre-RapidAI workflow.

echoes.setting: Hub-and-spoke stroke network in Texas, with a different product (Viz.ai LVO): the median time from CT angiography at the spoke hospital to arrival at the comprehensive stroke center fell from 132.5 to 110 minutes for 43 patients with large vessel occlusion (Hassan et al., Interventional Neuroradiology)

A single comprehensive stroke center that introduced RapidAI in June 2018: among 2,144 stroke admissions from 2014 to 2024, door-to-needle time showed no adjusted change after implementation, while length of stay and rescue craniectomy fell; the authors cite low software use and secular trends (González et al., Cerebrovascular Diseases, 19 October 2026)

fields.summary: RapidAI's large vessel occlusion alert prompted a physician to mobilize the stroke team for Eric, 29; thrombectomy restored flow under 60 minutes from arrival; no deficits.
fields.account: Memorial Healthcare System began a RapidAI trial at Memorial Regional Hospital in 2017, according to its release. It then extended the platform to Memorial Hospital West, Memorial Hospital Miramar and Memorial Hospital Pembroke. Eric, a 29-year-old firefighter and paramedic, felt unwell after a workout. He tried to send a text and could not move his left thumb, then his left leg went numb. His trainer noticed that he was slurring and called 9-1-1. Emergency medical services (EMS) took him to Memorial Hospital West's Comprehensive Stroke Center. Under the Memorial stroke protocol the paramedics had already alerted the hospital. The neurointerventional surgery team was ready to do a computed tomography (CT) scan and treat in the catheterization laboratory. As soon as scan results were available, Dr Brijesh Mehta received the RapidAI alert on his smartphone and smartwatch. It showed the software's automated detection of a large vessel occlusion (LVO). The alert prompted him to mobilize the catheterization laboratory team and fast-track Eric for mechanical thrombectomy. The blocked artery was fully opened and blood flow restored under 60 minutes from his arrival. Eric described himself as alive with no deficits. The hospital published the account on 12 May 2022. The release gives neither the date nor the city of Eric's stroke, and it gives no measured time saved by the alert.

produced_by: RapidAI LVO detection pushing alerts to the on-call neurointerventionalist's phone and watch
A comprehensive stroke center with an in-house thrombectomy team
must_hold: Rapid recognition of stroke signs and EMS transport to a thrombectomy-capable center
Team mobilization on the AI alert rather than after a formal radiology read

echoes.setting: Hub-and-spoke stroke network in Texas, with a different product (Viz.ai LVO): the median time from CT angiography at the spoke hospital to arrival at the comprehensive stroke center fell from 132.5 to 110 minutes for 43 patients with large vessel occlusion (Hassan et al., Interventional Neuroradiology)

A single comprehensive stroke center that introduced RapidAI in June 2018: among 2,144 stroke admissions from 2014 to 2024, door-to-needle time showed no adjusted change after implementation, while length of stay and rescue craniectomy fell; the authors cite low software use and secular trends (González et al., Cerebrovascular Diseases, 19 October 2026)
